name: Naturpark Zillertaler Alpen
kurzbeschreibung: The Naturpark Zillertaler Alpen is a protected high-alpine region featuring glaciers, peaks, and a rich diversity of flora and fauna.
beschreibung:
Overview

The High Alps Nature Park Zillertal Alps covers 379 square kilometers of pristine protected wilderness in the upper Zillertal valley, spanning from 1,000 meters elevation at the mountaineering village of Ginzling up to 3,509 meters on the glaciated summit of the Hochfeiler. Known as an alpine sanctuary of tranquility, this high-mountain reserve is completely free of ski lifts, cable cars, and commercial infrastructure. Instead, five magnificent glaciated tributary valleys—Zemmgrund, Stillupgrund, Zillergrund, Floitental, and Tuxertal—define its dramatic landscape. More than 80 glaciers, over 85 secluded alpine tarns, cascading glacial torrents, and rare arctic-alpine flora make the park an unrivaled haven for mountaineers and nature purists. The administrative nerve center is the Nature Park House in Ginzling, renowned for its rich mineral heritage and historic climbing expeditions.

Route & Requirements

The trail network spans historic hut approaches to epic multi-day alpine crossings. A world-famous classic is the trek to the heritage-listed Berliner Hütte (2,042 m) in Zemmgrund: departing Gasthof Breitlahner, a well-marked farm and alpine trail ascends past rustic chalets and cascading waterfalls into a magnificent glacial cirque to reach the grand, wood-paneled imperial mountain refuge (3 hours walking time, 790 m elevation gain, moderate grade T2). Another iconic outing is the climb from turquoise Lake Schlegeis to the Olpererhütte (2,389 m), famous for its suspension bridge suspended over the reservoir (1.5 to 2 hours, 600 m climb, paved granite step trail T2). For long-distance trekkers, the Berliner Höhenweg represents one of the premier alpine circuits in the Eastern Alps, connecting seven high-altitude mountain refuges over 7 to 8 demanding stages requiring surefootedness, head for heights, and stamina (rated T3/T4). Ankle-high mountaineering boots, rain protection, and sufficient provisions are vital. Dogs are permitted on trails, but strict overnight regulations apply inside mountain huts.

Visit & Arrival

Travelers arrive by rail via ÖBB or the scenic Zillertalbahn to Mayrhofen rail terminal. From Mayrhofen, regional VVT bus line 4102 runs hourly to Ginzling (Nature Park House stop). In summer, specialized alpine shuttles ferry hikers directly from Mayrhofen up to the high reservoir trailheads at Schlegeis, Zillergründl, and Stillup. Drivers follow the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Wiesing/Zillertal) and the B169 highway to Mayrhofen, continuing south via the mountain road to Ginzling and toll roads leading to the dams. Plentiful hiker parking is available in Ginzling and at Schlegeisspeicher.

Tips

Explore the "Hidden Treasures" exhibition inside the Nature Park House in Ginzling, displaying dazzling alpine smoky quartz crystals and garnets discovered by local mineral prospectors. To capture the famous photo on the suspension bridge beside the Olpererhütte without waiting in lines, hike up early in the morning or book an overnight stay at the hut to enjoy serene sunrise lighting.
